questions.stem: A company applying for a Massachusetts pharmacy licence has a minority investor whose previous out-of-state pharmacy entered a consent agreement resolving a complaint, and whose separate professional licence was once suspended. The applicant company itself has a clean record. Which statements about the Board's suitability review are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The factors reach an interest holder as well as the applicant itself.
A consent agreement resolving a complaint is among the listed factors.
Only conduct at a Massachusetts pharmacy may be weighed by the Board.
Prior discipline on a separate professional licence is a listed factor.
The Board may conclude that licensing would not serve public health and safety.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is being sold. Twenty days before the closing date the buyer submits a complete licence application with the controlled substance inventory report and the bill of sale. The seller files nothing, on the basis that the buyer's application tells the Board everything it needs. Is the seller's position sound?

choices.text: No, because the outgoing licensee owes the Board its own notice of the transfer.
No, because the seller must instead surrender the licence to the Board first.
Yes, because the buyer's application was filed more than 14 days ahead.
Yes, because the inventory report identifies both pharmacies to the Board.
Yes, provided the seller countersigns the buyer's licence application.

questions.stem: A closing Massachusetts pharmacy will move its Schedule II through VI stock to a sister pharmacy. The Manager of Record has given the Board written certified-mail notice with all required particulars and the transfer is set for day 15. Which statements about what follows are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The transferor may keep a small residual stock to finish outstanding prescriptions.
An attestation confirming the inventory is filed with the Board within 30 days.
The inventory covers Schedules II through V and reportable Schedule VI substances.
Only the transferee's Manager of Record needs to sign the inventory report.
The transferor may possess no controlled substances after the transfer date.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts sterile compounding applicant has held a provisional licence for eleven months. It has made real progress but will not reach full compliance for another two months, and asks the Board to extend the provisional licence for that period. What is the position?

choices.text: The Board may extend it once, for a period not exceeding six months.
The Board may extend it where the applicant shows continued substantial compliance.
The Board must extend it, since full compliance is the stated objective.
The Board may convert it now and inspect for full compliance afterwards.
The provisional licence may not be renewed or extended and lapses at one year.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts wholesale drug distributor changes its designated responsible person and its warehouse address. Its compliance officer plans to report both at the next annual renewal, and adds that a director's old felony conviction for an offence unrelated to drugs cannot matter to the Board. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: Both points are sound; renewal is the natural time to update the record.
The reporting plan is sound, but the conviction is a listed Board factor.
The changes go to the Board within 30 days, and any felony conviction is listed.
The changes go to the Board within 30 days, but the conviction falls outside the list.
Neither point matters, because the factors govern issuance rather than renewal.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts company holds a wholesale druggist controlled substance registration and is opening a second distribution warehouse in another city. Its counsel says the existing registration covers the new site and runs on the same two-year cycle as the group's pharmacy registrations. What is the position?

choices.text: Counsel is right on both points, since one registrant holds one registration.
Counsel is right on coverage but wrong on the cycle, which is three years.
Counsel is wrong on coverage but right that a two-year cycle applies.
Counsel is wrong on both: a separate registration is needed and the term is one year.
Counsel is wrong on coverage, and the wholesale registration has no fixed expiry.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts nuclear pharmacy is describing its services to a hospital client. Which activities fall inside the regulatory definition of radiopharmaceutical service? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Counting, dispensing, labeling and delivery of radiopharmaceuticals.
Operating the imaging equipment on which the product is later used.
Interpreting the images produced after the product is administered.
Prescribing the radiopharmaceutical for the individual hospital patient.
Advising on therapeutic values, hazards and use of radiopharmaceuticals.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts entity holds a provisional outsourcing facility registration because it had not been inspected by the FDA in the two years before its application. It has compounded a batch of sterile preparations and wants to ship them to a hospital in the Commonwealth while it waits for the inspection. May it?

choices.text: Yes, because the provisional registration authorises it to operate as a facility.
Yes, because the shipment stays inside the Commonwealth.
Yes, provided the receiving hospital records the provisional status.
No, because a provisional holder is barred from compounding until inspected.
No, because a provisional holder is permitted to compound but not to supply.

questions.stem: On a Monday a Massachusetts pharmacy discovers that a controlled substance package delivered the previous Wednesday shows signs of having been opened and resealed. Nothing is confirmed missing. The Manager of Record plans to investigate for a few days and then decide whether to report. What does the regulation require?

choices.text: A report to the Drug Control Program within 24 hours of Monday's discovery.
A report to the Board of Registration in Pharmacy within 24 hours of Monday.
A report to the Drug Control Program within 24 hours of the Wednesday delivery.
No report, because no controlled substance has been confirmed missing.
A report once the internal investigation establishes that a loss occurred.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy's computerized system cannot show what it previously dispensed to a patient until an overnight batch runs, so at the counter the pharmacist cannot see the patient's earlier fills. The pharmacy says its staff always ask patients thoroughly about their history. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Thorough questioning satisfies the retrieval requirement, since the goal is the same.
The retrieval requirement is measured by reasonable effort, as the content duty is.
The system must allow immediate retrieval when the prescription is presented.
A pharmacy may rely on the overnight batch if it documents the limitation.
Institutional sterile compounding pharmacies are outside these requirements.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts collaborative practice agreement was properly written, signed and within the supervising physician's scope when it was made twenty-six months ago. Neither party has reviewed it since. The pharmacist proposes to keep co-managing referred patients while a review is scheduled. What is the position?

choices.text: The agreement stands, because nothing in it has changed since it was signed.
The agreement stands, provided the pharmacist documents that a review is pending.
The agreement stands until the supervising physician gives notice of termination.
The agreement is out of currency, because review and renewal fall due biennially.
The agreement is void, and every act taken under it in month 25 must be reported.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy makes its offer to counsel by printing a line on the receipt inviting the patient to ask for the pharmacist. Its manager says the statute leaves the method open so long as the patient learns the offer is available. A second patient that day is deaf and cannot use the telephone. What does the statute provide?

choices.text: Any method reaching the patient qualifies, so the receipt line is sufficient.
The offer is made face to face or by telephone, with an alternative where needs require.
The offer must be made face to face in every case, so the telephone is not available.
A printed offer qualifies where the pharmacy also posts a patient rights sign.
The pharmacy may decline to counsel the second patient because of the barrier.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts hospital pharmacy dispenses to inpatients on the wards and also operates an outpatient window in the lobby. Its director asks which prospective drug review and counselling duties under the statute apply where. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The section applies in full to inpatients, since the pharmacy is licensed by the Board.
The section does not apply to a drug dispensed to an inpatient at a hospital.
The inpatient carve-out yields where federal regulations require otherwise.
The carve-out reaches the outpatient window as well, since it is the same pharmacy.
A nursing home dispensing falls outside the carve-out, which names hospitals alone.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy's label printer fails on a Saturday afternoon with patients waiting. The pharmacist writes labels by hand, in clear block capitals, for the remainder of the shift and again on Monday because the queue is long, although the printer was repaired that morning. How should the two days be assessed?

choices.text: Saturday is permitted as an emergency period; Monday is not.
Both days are permitted, because each label was legibly written.
Both days fail, because a label must always be computer printed.
Saturday fails as well, unless the Board approved the handwriting in advance.
Monday is permitted, because a queue is itself an emergency for this purpose.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist dispenses a product distributed solely under its generic name. The package carries no NDC number. The pharmacist can see the manufacturer's name on the carton and also has the repacker's name on the invoice. What must be recorded in the computerized pharmacy system?

choices.text: Either name, since the purpose is to identify the product dispensed.
The repacker's name, which is the entity that supplied this pharmacy.
Both names, so that the chain of supply is recorded in full.
The manufacturer's name, the repacker being a later fallback.
Neither name; the pharmacist records the generic name and strength.

questions.stem: A prescriber's office telephones a Massachusetts pharmacy with a new prescription while the pharmacist on duty is counselling another patient. Which statements about who may take the call are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Only the pharmacist may take a new prescription by telephone.
Any pharmacy employee may take it and pass it to the pharmacist to check.
A pharmacy intern may receive a new prescription over the telephone.
An uncertified technician may take it provided the pharmacist verifies it afterwards.
A certified technician with the on-duty pharmacist's approval may receive it.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts prescription was written on 1 March. A patient presents it and the pharmacist must decide whether it is still within a thirty-day window. Which date is the last day on which it remains within date?

choices.text: 30 March, counting 1 March as day one of the period.
31 March, counting 2 March as day one of the period.
1 April, because a partial first day is disregarded entirely.
29 March, because both the first and the last day are excluded.
It cannot be determined without knowing the schedule of the drug.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy receives filled and labelled vials from a central facility in another state that is not licensed by the Board. On arrival the pharmacist inspects each vial against the prescription and finds everything correct. May the pharmacy dispense them?

choices.text: Yes, because the pharmacist has personally checked each finished product.
Yes, because central fill is a recognised part of ordinary pharmacy practice.
No, unless the process was verified by a Massachusetts licensed pharmacist.
No, because a pharmacy may never dispense what it did not process itself.
No, unless the receiving pharmacy documents the inspection in the patient profile.

questions.stem: An agent collecting a Schedule IV prescription for a housebound Massachusetts patient has no government identification with her. The pharmacist believes refusing would cause the patient real hardship. Which statements about dispensing without a Customer Identifier are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacist's belief about hardship is by itself sufficient.
The reason for dispensing without an identifier must be documented.
A regular patient known to the pharmacy is outside the requirement.
The agent must print her name and address and sign for the dispensing.
The requirement reaches Schedule VI dispensings on the same terms.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is filling a written prescription for a controlled substance dispensed as capsules. Which items must appear on the label the pharmacist affixes to the container? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The prescribing practitioner's registration number.
The filling pharmacist's initials.
The serial number of the prescription.
The number of capsules in the container.
The date of filling, and the pharmacy name and address.

questions.stem: An eighty-two year old Massachusetts patient collects a prescription and says nothing about the label. The pharmacy's policy is to print all labels in its standard size. A second patient the same day asks for larger directions because of impaired vision. What does the statute require?

choices.text: Nothing for the first patient; typed directions at no more than ten characters per inch for the second.
Enlarged directions for both, since the first patient is plainly elderly.
Nothing for either, because the statute governs the pharmacy's own type standard.
Enlarged directions for the second patient only if a prescriber orders them.
Enlarged print across the entire label for the second patient, not the directions alone.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist takes an oral controlled-substance prescription from a caller she has never dealt with, reduces it to writing at once, and dispenses. Eight days later no electronic prescription has arrived and the prescriber holds no commissioner exception from electronic prescribing. What has gone wrong?

choices.text: Nothing; the pharmacist's written record is the complete requirement.
Only that the pharmacist should have refused an oral prescription outright.
Only that the written record should have been made within two days rather than at once.
The pharmacist should have obtained the prescription in writing before dispensing.
No reasonable effort was made to verify the caller, and the two-day follow-up has lapsed.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy fills a written Schedule II prescription. The technician files it with the Schedule III and IV prescriptions, and the label carries the filling pharmacist's initials but the prescription itself bears no signature other than the prescriber's. What is missing?

choices.text: Nothing; the initials on the label record who filled the prescription.
Only the separate file, the prescriber's signature being the one required.
Only the pharmacist's endorsement, Schedule II filing being at the pharmacy's discretion.
A second pharmacist's countersignature verifying the Schedule II dispensing.
The filling pharmacist's endorsement on the face, and the separate Schedule II file.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy wants to hire a warehouse assistant who will work beside the controlled-substance cage. Eleven years ago his own registration was revoked for a regulatory violation; he has worked without incident since. The pharmacy proposes to hire him and document the history. What does the regulation permit?

choices.text: Hiring is permitted, because eleven incident-free years have passed.
Hiring is permitted if the pharmacy keeps him away from the cage itself.
Hiring is permitted once the Commissioner is notified of the history.
Hiring is barred, because a revoked registration disqualifies him at any time.
Hiring is barred unless a second registrant vouches for his trustworthiness.

questions.stem: Three Massachusetts-licensed pharmacies are closing on the same date: a non-resident Drug Store pharmacy, a resident sterile compounding pharmacy, and an institutional sterile compounding pharmacy. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Each must give the Board certified written notice at least 14 days before closing.
The non-resident pharmacy must make the post-closure submission of original licences.
The sterile compounding pharmacy must identify a pharmacy able to continue patient care.
The institutional sterile compounding pharmacy is excused from the patient-notice duty.
The continuity-of-care pharmacy identified must be licensed by the Board.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy has signed a lease on premises two doors along and plans to move in five weeks. Its manager will write to the Board a week beforehand describing the new layout. What does the regulation require?

choices.text: Written notice a week ahead is sufficient for a move within the same block.
Board approval before relocating, on an application filed at least 90 days ahead.
Board approval before relocating, on an application filed at least 14 days ahead.
Nothing before the move, provided the new address is reported within 14 days.
A fresh licence application, the existing licence lapsing on the day of the move.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts Drug Store pharmacy is enlarging its prescription area by taking in an adjoining storeroom. The contractor is ready and the pharmacy files its application on the morning work is due to begin, enclosing drawings of the new prescription area. What is wrong?

choices.text: Work may not commence until approval, and the counselling area must be depicted too.
Nothing, provided the pharmacy stops work if the Board later raises an objection.
Only that the drawings must be certified by an architect for a Drug Store pharmacy.
Only that a change of square footage requires a fresh licence rather than approval.
Only that the application should have gone to the Department rather than the Board.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts sterile compounding pharmacy is replacing an ageing cleanroom air handling unit with an identical new one in the same position. Its director says a like-for-like swap changes nothing and needs no filing. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A like-for-like replacement falls outside the approval requirement.
Board approval is required before replacing any secondary engineering control.
Ordinary layout drawings suffice, since the configuration is unchanged.
The submission includes certified blueprints with ISO classification of each control.
Approval may be sought after the work if the pharmacy suspends compounding.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy's Manager of Record is leaving amicably at the end of the month and a successor has been identified. Which statements about the change of Manager of Record application are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The inventory attestation is signed by both the outgoing and the incoming Manager.
The inventory covers Schedules II through V and reportable Schedule VI substances.
A staff pharmacist may sign in place of the outgoing Manager for convenience.
The original Drug Store Pharmacy licence accompanies the application.
The Board may require the proposed Manager of Record to appear before it.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy rebrands and begins trading under a new name on 1 June. The licence holder, the premises and the ownership are all unchanged. The manager plans to mention the new name in the pharmacy's next annual renewal filing in November. What does the regulation require?

choices.text: Nothing further, since the licence holder and premises are unchanged.
Notice at the next renewal, which is what the regulation contemplates.
Written notice to the Board within 14 days, with authorizing documentation.
Written notice to the Board within 90 days, as for a change of location.
A fresh licence application, the old trading name having been surrendered.
